newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond spreads widen at the close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond spreads widen at the close.

text.p: Some late weakness in the Australian bond market saw an initial narrowing of spreads to the U.S. and Canada reversed and turned into widenings.

Despite being weaker from the open in line with softer Treasuries, bonds were outperforming their North American counterparts in early trading, with the spread to U.S. 10-years touching 100 basis points.

However, the late afternoon selling, which traders said was exaggerated by the thin market conditions, saw seven point losses on the 10 year futures contract grow to 17, and the opening spread gains reversed.
Spreads to N.Z. bonds also widened, after the release of the Reserve Bank monetary policy statement saw bonds there sold off bu trecover by the close.
The initial reaction flowed from RBNZ Governor Don Brash's statement that markets had been "somewhat excessive" in their reaction to the formation of a centre-right coaltion government last week.

However, a stronger N.Z. dollar and a closer examination of what had been said saw the market recover by the close, traders said. Combined with the local weakness, it saw the NZ long bond yield fall back under its Australian counterpart.
